Verification highlights: (1) FINAL_STATES: u4 is present, declared in STATES, and accepting — u4 is reachable only via target_picked_up, which is exactly the task's terminating event. (2) The two-move key-hold requirement is correctly gated before the box: u3 is reachable only from u1 via (has_door_key & door_open) or from u2 via door_open; both entry paths imply has_door_key held at two distinct steps (the u0->u1 pickup step and the following evaluation), since u1 is evaluated exactly one step after key pickup and u2's entry requires a second hold. Because any door-opening episode necessarily carries the key on the pickup step through the toggle step (>=2 consecutive holds), every box-taking trajectory reaches u3 and then u4, and no trajectory can reach u4 with fewer than two key-holding moves — u4 holds iff the task is satisfied. (3) Regression handling is correct where required: u1 -key_lost-> u0 resets when the key is dropped before the two-move hold is achieved, while u2 and u3 correctly do NOT regress on key_lost — the two-move hold is an achievement (sticky via else), and after door_open the agent must drop the key before picking up the box, so a key_lost regression from u3 would make the task unsatisfiable in the RM. The sticky u3 also correctly handles traces where the agent closes the door behind it before picking up the box. (4) Reward safety: rewards 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.2 / 1.0 are each earned at most once (no state permits returning to u1 or re-firing u2->u3), total is bounded at 1.3, and the two paths to u3 are reward-consistent (direct u1->u3 = 0.3 equals u1->u2->u3 = 0.1+0.2). Progress rewards are dense across the three milestones with no reward on irrelevant steps, and else self-loops in all five states cover irrelevant events for totality. (5) Labels use only the four given propositions with boolean connectives; key_lost is correctly treated as a one-step event trigger, conditions as level-triggered guards; the transition function is deterministic (key_lost excludes has_door_key and door_open, and the two has_door_key guards at u1 are disjoint). All five states are reachable. Minor non-blocking notes: the (u1, else) self-loop is unreachable in practice (from u1 the next step is always u0 via key_lost, u2, or u3), and the candidate counts the two key-holds as consecutive steps rather than arbitrary distinct steps — this is immaterial here since door opening forces consecutive holds, so neither acceptance semantics nor the final reward is affected.
